Package dyntabs.ai.decision

Class Decisions

java.lang.Object
dyntabs.ai.decision.Decisions
public final class Decisions extends Object
The answers from one EasyAI.decide(...) call — one entry per question you asked.

Why this wrapper exists (it is not cosmetic)

The underlying answers carry a real trap: probabilities are optional. When the model does not report them, the raw probabilityOf(...) and margin() accessors throw IllegalStateException, and confidence() can be null. Code written against the happy path looks correct, passes review, and fails in production on the first answer that arrives without probabilities.

So every accessor here that can be absent returns OptionalDouble instead of throwing, and the ones that are always present return a plain double. The type tells you which is which, at compile time.

Thresholds are deliberate, never defaulted

There is no isYes(name) — only isYes(String, double). A yes/no answer is a probability, and turning a probability into a decision means choosing a line. That line is a business judgement, so the API makes you write it down where a reviewer can see it. "A measured probability crossed a threshold I chose" is a defensible sentence; "the AI decided" is not.

Mistakes are named, not cryptic

Asking for a question you never asked, or reading a choice answer as yes/no, fails with a message that names the question and lists what is actually available — rather than a ClassCastException or a null.


 Decisions d = EasyAI.decide(ticketText)
     .yesNo("urgent",   "Is the customer blocked from working?")
     .choice("team",    "Which team should handle this?", "billing", "technical", "sales")
     .scale("severity", "How severe is the impact?", "low", "medium", "high")
     .ask();

 if (d.isYes("urgent", 0.80)) pager.wake();        // the 0.80 is YOUR call, in the open
 route(d.choice("team"));
 double severity = d.mean("severity");             // 0.0 .. levels-1, can land between levels

 d.margin("team").ifPresent(m -> { if (m < 0.15) queueForHuman(); });   // only if reported

Analogy: a lab report. It states each measurement and its confidence; it does not tell you whether to operate. The threshold for acting is the clinician's, written in the notes.

    • isYes

      public boolean isYes(String name, double threshold)
      Turn a yes/no probability into a decision at your threshold.
      Parameters:
      name - the question name you used when asking
      threshold - the probability at or above which this counts as "yes", between 0.0 and 1.0
      Returns:
      true if the reported probability reaches threshold
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if threshold is outside 0.0–1.0, or the question is unknown or was not a yes/no question

    • mean

      public double mean(String name)
      The position of a scale answer across the levels you offered, as a probability-weighted index.

      It can land between two levels — with levels low, medium, high a mean of 1.4 means "somewhere between medium and high, closer to medium". That in-between value is the point of a scale question; rounding it away throws the information out.

      Parameters:
      name - the question name
      Returns:
      the weighted index, from 0.0 to levels - 1

    • isRefused

      public boolean isRefused(String name)
      Whether the model declined to answer a particular question.

      Check this before reading an answer when a question could touch content the model refuses to judge; reading a refused answer is an error, not an empty result.

      Parameters:
      name - the question name
      Returns:
      true if the model refused this question

    • summary

      public String summary()
      A short, readable line per answer — what gets logged or shown in an activity timeline.
